messages.author: 8f8b5832b9ad8628
messages.subject: Don't estimate intercepts for dummies
parts:
Dear All,

Do please forgive my simplistic question. But in my reproducible example below, is it possible NOT to estimate the intercepts for the dummy variables Group_HI and Group_MT? 

(In fact, is it necessary to estimate them?)

Many thanks,

library(tidyverse); library(fastDummies)

d <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rnorouzian/v/main/memory.csv")
d <- dummy_cols(d, "Group")[-7]

model <- "MP ~ Group_HI
   SE ~  Group_HI
   MP ~  Group_MT
   SE ~  Group_MT
   Group_HI ~~ 0*Group_MT
   MP ~~ MP
   SE ~~ SE
   MP ~~ SE"

sem(model, data = d, meanstructure = TRUE)

Intercepts:
                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)
   .MP                4.667    0.466   10.018    0.000
   .SE                4.200    0.256   16.413    0.000
    Group_HI          0.385    0.067    5.701    0.000
    Group_MT          0.327    0.065    5.026    0.000

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Don't estimate intercepts for dummies
parts: The dummies in your model appear to be exogenous, so what's listed under intercepts are effectively raw means. So yes, it is necessary to estimate them, but it doesn't "cost" anything to do so.

messages.author: 8f8b5832b9ad8628
messages.subject: Re: Don't estimate intercepts for dummies
parts:
Dear Patrick,

Thanks. May I follow up on that:

tl;dr: Group_HI ~~ 0*Group_MT  #Question: what is the effect of removing this line on SE of regression coefs?

Imagine I remove the `Group_HI ~~ 0*Group_MT` altogether. What is the difference between a model that uses `Group_HI ~~ 0*Group_MT` and one that doesn't include anything to describe the relation between Group_HI and Group_MT?

Specifically, it seems the latter produces Standard Errors for coefs that are closer to those given by a MANOVA: ( 
summary(lm(cbind(MP,SE)~Group,data=d)) ). 

But the former produces Standard Errors for coefs that are closer to those given by: (

stacked_DVs <- pivot_longer(d, c(MP,SE), names_to = "DV")
coef(summary(lm(value~DV*Group-1,data = stacked_DVs)))  ).

#=== Reproducible data and code

library(tidyverse); library(fastDummies)

d <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rnorouzian/v/main/memory.csv")
d <- dummy_cols(d, "Group")[-5]

model <- "MP ~ Group_HI
   SE ~  Group_HI
   MP ~  Group_MT
   SE ~  Group_MT
### Group_HI ~~ 0*Group_MT  #Question: what is the effect of removing this line on SE of coefs?

MP ~~ MP
   SE ~~ SE
   MP ~~ SE"

fit = sem(model, data = d, meanstructure = TRUE)
summary(fit)

The dummies in your model appear to be exogenous, so what's listed under intercepts are effectively raw means. So yes, it is necessary to estimate them, but it doesn't "cost" anything to do so.

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Don't estimate intercepts for dummies
parts: It's rarely a good idea to constrain variances on exogenous variables at all, and sem() defaults to freeing them all (as does every SEM package, as far as I know). And dummy codes are intrinsically correlated. I don't see any benefit.
